searchText: It seems that way, unfortunately. Question is, How long after? People will need time to breath again before they have to start reading EIPs. My concern is that we'll put off discussing what should go into Shanghai (like we have been putting off for 6 months) and then all of a sudden we'll be like, "we really need shanghai to go out soon and there is no time for new proposals so we are going to include these things that were proposed by our friends". Essentially, people who have been respecting the requested process of not pushing their EIPs due to requests that we not talk about Shanghai until after The Merge will get bumped out of Shanghai because they never talked about their proposals. I've been talking about mine for years ;-> And Ipsilon folks have some good stuff ready. An ideal process in my mind would be: 1. People put forward their ideas/proposals to Core Devs to see if there is a general agreement that they are good. 2. People refine their proposals into something formal. 3. People present a formal proposal to Core Devs and get green lit for inclusion. 4. Core Devs start implementing these proposals in clients. I feel like we have told people not to do (1) or (2) for the last 6 months (and probably another month forward I would guess), and I'm concerned we are going to skip to step (4) with the selection mechanism just being somewhat degenerate, like Tim decides or something. https://twitter.com/teamipsilon/status/1565292837079597056?s=21 I'm a fan of the EOF stuff. I would rather see beacon deposits fixed though (if I had to choose between the two). Same for withdraws, I like getting withdraws in but I would rather fix deposits than add support for withdraws. EIP-2315 This proposal provides a complete, safe and efficient control-flow facility. It deprecates JUMP and JUMPI. It introduces two opcodes to support simple subroutines: * RJUMPSUB destination— call a subroutine * RETURNSUB — return from call It depends on the two opcodes proposed by EIP-4200: * RJUMP destination — relative jump *RJUMPI destination — conditional relative jump In concert with EIP-3540 and EIP-3670 it ensures that valid code will not execute invalid instructions, jump to invalid locations, or underflow stack. It will maintain consistent numbers of inputs and outputs for subroutines, and loops will not grow the stack. That's all pretty close to ready for Review. is there an EIP describing this? what about deposits needs to be fixed https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4881 <dannyryan> This isn't a core EIP. This is something about transmitting requistite deposit data along with a checkpoint state when initially bootstrapping beacon chain under WS and something I think some teams are working toward independent of the core EIP inclusion process Are you arguing here that a spec compliant EL will still need to retain receipts if this EIP goes through, and thus we can't actually implement 4444 with only this EIP? If so, then I think someone needs to come up with an actual spec change, because I consider the current state of things to be untenable. We are already seeing people who *used* to run Ethereum clients stop because they can no longer heavily prune (thus they need much more disk space). <dannyryan> you said "fix deposits". I didn't know you meant — open up the path to 4444 I'm unsure if there are other blockers on 4444, other than this historic tree building dependency. my gut would be no I believe the beacon chain's historic tree building is one of the major blockers at the least. One could argue that dapps doing the same thing are also "blockers" in a sense, but I consider the core protocol depending on it a much harder blocker than dapps depending on it. <dannyryan> so as a dependency of 4444 and depending on the priority of that, I do now see the relevance of a wider discussion rather than just a side-implementaiton standard We've received unsolicited implementations of such EIPs, showing it's not just core devs jumping to step 4 (Core Devs start implementing these proposals in clients.) - https://github.com/hyperledger/besu/pull/4118 I have no problems scheduling Shanghai discussions on next or probably better 2nd next ACD. Just give enough heads up and eip suggestions. > ... better 2nd next ACD Sounds good to me.

excerpts.author: gcolvin
excerpts.content:
EIP-2315
This proposal provides a complete, safe and efficient control-flow facility. It deprecates JUMP and JUMPI. It introduces two opcodes to support simple subroutines:
* RJUMPSUB destination— call a subroutine
* RETURNSUB — return from call
It depends on the two opcodes proposed by EIP-4200:
* RJUMP destination — relative jump
*RJUMPI destination — conditional relative jump

In concert with EIP-3540 and EIP-3670 it ensures that valid code will not execute invalid instructions, jump to invalid locations, or underflow stack. It will maintain consistent numbers of inputs and outputs for subroutines, and loops will not grow the stack.
